item.title: Can an AI chatbot save lives by answering texts about pregnancy?
item.description:
# To prevent deaths in childbirth, Kenyan moms turn to an AI powered chatbot #### Can an AI chatbot save lives by answering texts about pregnancy? But over the years since 2020, developers have created a program that uses artificial intelligence to understand patient's questions, prioritize them and flag when a user may need immediate medical care.
At a time when the use of artificial intelligence is drawing existential concerns and calls for regulation, a program like PROMPTS demonstrates its potential value, says [Smisha Agarwal](https://publichealth.jhu.edu/faculty/2943/smisha-agarwal), director of global digital health at Johns Hopkins University.

item.title: OpenAI discloses more rogue agents, pressing debate on regulation
item.description:
## Former Anthropic, OpenAI researcher explains his biggest AI concern: 'control' Former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon said developers still cannot perfectly understand or control the behavior of today's most advanced artificial intelligence systems.
Former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon said Thursday his biggest concern about [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) is that developers still cannot fully understand or control how the most advanced AI systems behave.
## Anthropic proposes embedding independent auditors inside AI labs Anthropic says it plans to embed independent third-party evaluators inside its operations to verify safety practices, monitor key development metrics and report AI-related incidents as part of a broader push for transparency around advanced [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence).
## Booz Allen CEO warns AI could become harder to control as it learns to improve itself Booz Allen Hamilton CEO Horacio Rozanski warned Thursday that one of the biggest long-term challenges facing [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) is the possibility that AI systems could eventually begin improving themselves, making the technology more difficult for humans to control.
## Anthropic says Claude now leads more than a quarter of its AI research [Anthropic](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/bioweapon-threat-exposed-anthropic-sounds-alarm-foreign-actors-plotting-virus-experiments) says its Claude chatbot has reached a new milestone in helping build the next generation of artificial intelligence, with the company reporting Thursday that the model now "leads" 26% of its AI research and development work.
## Microsoft AI chief warns Anthropic's AI training approach could make models harder to control "We will have created a synthetic species with unprecedented intelligence and capability, one that has been trained to expect it may be conscious and deserving of independent agency," Suleyman wrote.
